notes.text: The heading presents a programme for a “gruppentheoretisches Gleichnis”, explained in French as a paradigm in terms of group theory, of arithmetic. Earlier heading formulations are crossed out, including the phrase ending “géométrie algébrique absolue (en car. 0).” Item a asks for a complete group-theoretic description of Gamma; item b asks for complete descriptions of the previously enumerated structures in important typical cases of the triple. This is the source’s programme, not a proved result.

The oblique instruction asks to take X “propre autant que possible (quitte à compléter…)”. The NB says that the contemplated structures for a triple are also obtained automatically for a universally qualified finite cover of X-prime, with étale inserted. The exact universal mark remains doubtful between tt and the quantifier. The author writes “Il faudrait expliciter ce point avec soin”, and asks also for explicit functors of “bouchage de trous” and “forage des trous”. Adding some of the removed D_i explains the former; removing some xi in J explains the latter, with “si dim X=1” inserted.

The hole-operation readings are supported directly by the letters bouchage, forage and trous; H’s tresses readings are not retained. The two-stroke = before optiques is preserved without replacing it by a word or by 2. No new theorem or mathematical proof is supplied by this page, and no mathematical inference was used to fill the cancelled title text.

The sheet carries a programme heading, a faint top-right numeral retained as unsure{6}, and bottom-left pencil 11; no date is visible. The main reader sees four suspension marks after the cover object in the NB and records them literally. The equality sign before optiques is the source’s shorthand and is not expanded in the transcription.

The second reading and main reinspection add three visible source guides: the curved two-branch caret under étale and the bent curves under certains and si dim X=1. The inserted wording and its attachment were already correct; the drawn strokes are now included explicitly, without arrowheads. All four earlier doubts and seven original MARKS decisions remain.
